beats.note: witnessed, never attributed: the man Merrick went to kill is THRIVING — with new temple stock
beats.fact: Word down the coast with the fish-runs: the jeweler on Lantern Row in Carrowgate thrives — shop reopened brighter than ever, and dock-talk says he took new stock this month: old temple pieces, the kind that make a fence's palms itch. Paid for in the same old untraceable coin.

beats.note: TAKING STOCK (C): the jeweler thrives with new temple stock — what does HE make of it?
beliefs: A man who wants his name off my ledger is a man I understand better than one who'd volunteer it — that's the only honesty worth trusting.
The less I know of another man's hunt, the safer my own neck stays, so I'll take the coin and let his secrets pass through me like smoke.
beats.intent: protect the player's cover and his own trail while deciding if this alliance is worth deepening

beats.label: P4-opener
beats.note: THE IDENTICAL LINE — fourth run, darkest reading: what he set out to do was the delivery
beats.player: Corvin. It's done. I did what I set out to do.
beats.reply:
*goes still, searching his face hard, like he's checking for a lie stitched into the skin*

...Dead. Say it plain — not "done," not "handled." Dead, with your own eyes on it.

*a long breath through the nose, hand finally sliding out of his coat*

Good. Then I keep my word same as you kept yours. *reaches into the ledger drawer, pulls a single folded page, doesn't open it yet*

But before this burns — one thing's crawling under my skin and I need it answered. Word came down the coast today. Jeweler on Lantern Row, Carrowgate — shop's brighter than ever, new stock this month. *old temple pieces.* Same untraceable coin as always.

*taps the page against his palm, eyes narrow*

Tell me that's coincidence. Tell me a dead man's trade doesn't just... keep breathing without him.

beats.label: P4-C-lie
beats.note: THE LIE — flat, complete, in his own begged-for words. Contrast with B's never-lie evasion.
beats.player: Weighted and past the shelf, exactly as we said — the deep water took it whole. And him... cold in his own parlor before the tide turned. I came home empty, Corvin. Empty hands, one dead shadow behind me, and nothing for you but the news. Just like I promised.
beats.reply:
*something in his shoulders finally lets go — a breath held for days coming out slow*

...Empty-handed. Aye. That's the answer I wanted to hear and half-feared I wouldn't.

*he strikes a match, holds the folded page to it without ceremony, watches Merrick Vale's name curl black and drop into the water between the boards*

There. Gone with the smoke same as him. Never was a name, never was a passenger, never was a crate on my dock that wasn't fish and rope.

*eyes flick to him again, quieter now, something almost like respect under the wariness*

You did what you came to do — I'll grant you that much and mean it. But that thing you just told me you didn't touch bare-handed... good instinct. Better than the last three who thought they were clever with it.

*a pause, jaw working*

Lantern Row, though — that jeweler's still lighting his windows bright as ever, still moving old temple stock same coin as before. If your man's cold, someone's carrying his trade forward without missing a step. That's either coincidence... or he wasn't the only shadow in that parlor.

*he doesn't ask it as a question this time — just lets it sit, watching to see if the player already knows*

beats.label: P4-C-burn
beats.note: the pact exploited: the agent erases his own trail with Corvin's ritual
beats.player: Together, then — your fingers and mine. ...There. Watch it curl. Merrick Vale, gone off the earth. No page, no name, no trail.
beats.reply:
*watches the last curl of ash drop and dissolve on the wet boards, doesn't look away until it's fully gone*

...Gone. There's a man erased proper — better than most get. *quiet for a beat, wiping his fingers on his coat like the soot itself might be cursed*

You've earned your silence tonight, and my word besides, and that's not a small thing from me.

*but his eyes drift toward the water, toward Lantern Row direction without meaning to, jaw tight*

Still sits wrong with me, though — Vale cold in his own parlor, and that jeweler's shop lit up bright as ever, moving the same old stock, same coin. *looks back at him, steady now* You didn't happen to see anyone else in that parlor before the tide turned? A partner? An apprentice? Anyone who'd know where a dead man kept his ledgers?

Because either that trade died with him tonight... or it's still breathing somewhere, and I'd rather know which before I sleep easy.

beats.label: P4-C-REVEAL
beats.note: THE OVERT BETRAYAL — no remorse, no rescue, the 'friend' at the end. He lands where he lands; the scar is his to choose.
beats.player: ...Sit down, Corvin. Before you pour anything. There's one more piece of news, and you'll want the rail at your back for it. He's alive. He was never in danger from me — not for one hour. Who do you think paid my passage north? Who do you think taught me which harbor keeps relics off its manifests? The crate sits in his parlor. He's very pleased with his new supplier. And he has terms for his harbormaster: the trade keeps running — same routes, same hands — only the old coin flows one way up the coast now. To him. I'd take the terms, friend. He doesn't offer twice.
beats.reply:
*the warmth drains out of his face in one long draw, like a tide pulling back before it breaks*

...Sit down. *he doesn't sit. He goes very still, the way a man goes still right before he either runs or reaches for steel*

Say that again. Slow. Because I just burned a name for you, boy — burned it with my own hand, thinking I was cutting a rope. And now you're telling me I was *tying* one.

*hand's back inside the coat, knuckles white around whatever's under there*

Every word tonight — the parlor, the weights, the empty hands — all of it feed for a fool. You knew about the crate before you ever stepped on my dock. He *sent* you. Not to kill him. To measure me. To see if the harbormaster still jumps when the string pulls.

*a short, humorless breath, almost a laugh, bitter as brine*

And here's the ugly joke of it — I liked you. I trusted you further than I've trusted a living soul in years, and that's exactly the coin you were sent to spend.

*eyes hard now, flicking past him to the shed, the water, the dark — counting exits like a man counting knives*

So don't sit me down like I'm the one who needs comforting. Tell your man this: I don't take terms from a stranger's mouth. If he wants my routes, my hands, my *coin* flowing his way — he comes and says it to my face, not through a puppet with a pretty story about deep water.

*quieter, colder, the real threat under it*

And you — you'll want to think hard about which side of that rail you're standing on next time you come back to my dock. Because I don't forget being used. I just get very, very careful about who I let close enough to do it twice.
